notes: (Top-level keys deliberately avoid `objects`/`contexts`, which other scripts read from curated/*.json.) Merge-layer fixes owned by the KB build (script/journeys/build_kb.ts), applied AFTER the curated tier. Curator files stay untouched; every entry says why. objectFixes.<id>: `patch` uses the curated merge semantics (plain objects replace wholesale, `facts` merge per key, null deletes); `journeyIneligible` keeps the record for the inspector but demotes provenance.status to 'seeded' with the reason in provenance.ineligibleReason. contextFixes.<id>.addMembers adds membership links (mirrored into each object's contextIds). Positions are fixed upstream in make_object_list.py (NGC 2527, Coalsack) and names of BSC stars there too (HR 6165 = tau Sco, HR 2890 = Castor B).

HR4210.why: Eta Carinae has brightened since the 1990s (its own deeper text says so): BSC5 V 6.21 is a 1940s-1990s value, which also kept it from closing a journey (PAYOFF_STAR_MAG 6.0). V is about 4.3 since 2018 (AAVSO light curve; Wikipedia, Eta Carinae).

radiusRsun.note: best-fitting O-star radius 22.3 ± 1.8 R☉ at 2.22 kpc (supplementary text)

lumLsun.note: log L/L☉ = 5.63 +0.07/−0.08 with Teff 31.1 ± 0.7 kK (supplementary text)

teffK.note: Teff = 31.1 ± 0.7 kK adopted in the dynamical model

HD226868.why: review panel 2026-11-02: the auto tier derived L = 13,000 L☉ and R = 4.8 R☉ with A_V = 0, but HDE 226868 is reddened by E(B−V) ≈ 1 (B−V 0.81 for an O9.7 supergiant), so both were ~30× and ~5× too small and produced false transitions ('about 40 times smaller than Deneb'). Values replaced with the cited paper's own (arXiv 2102.09091).

HR5267.why: review panel 2026-11-02: the derived luminosity used BC_V for 33,250 K while the adopted Teff is 25,000 K (Pigulski 2016), roughly doubling L; the Stefan–Boltzmann radius inherits the error. No sourced replacement in the KB, so both are removed.

HR1712.why: review panel 2026-11-02: L derived with A_V = 0 for a star reddened by E(B−V) ≈ 0.5 (L several times too small, R = 2.9 R☉ for an O9.5 V star). Removed until a sourced value is curated.

HR1203.why: review panel 2026-11-02: L derived with A_V = 0 for ζ Per, reddened by E(B−V) ≈ 0.3; removed until a sourced value is curated (the interferometric radius stays).

HR6736.why: review panel 2026-11-02: L derived with A_V = 0 for 9 Sgr inside the Lagoon (E(B−V) ≈ 0.3); R = 8 R☉ inherits it. Removed until a sourced value is curated.

HR2890.journeyIneligible: Castor B lies 5 arcsec from Castor A, so binoculars always show the pair as one point; Castor A (HR2891) carries the system on its card.

DS-OmSgr.journeyIneligible: Listed as a double-star target, but WDS has no companion for omega Sgr: the nearby stars are the unrelated corners of the Terebellum. Re-curate as a single star before journey use.
DS-OmSgr.why: curator-summer-south-stars flag; stars.auto has no WDS pair for HR 7597

HR5460.journeyIneligible: Alpha Centauri B lies about 8 arcsec from Alpha Centauri A, so binoculars always show the pair as one point; Alpha Centauri (HR5459) carries the system on its card.
HR5460.why: engine evaluation (docs/sky-journeys/engine-eval.md): same case as Castor B; the engine's same-sight rule already refused both components in one journey, but B alone was used as a stop

HR4731.journeyIneligible: Alpha-2 Crucis lies 3.5 arcsec from Acrux A, so binoculars always show the pair as one point; Acrux (HR4730) carries the system on its card.
HR4731.why: engine evaluation (docs/sky-journeys/engine-eval.md): same case as Castor B

IC1396.why: The auto tier matched HR24/OpenNGC rows for Trumpler 37 / the 14'x4' OpenNGC IC 1396 entry, which describe the central cluster and disagree with the curated 925 pc distance (curator note on facts.distanceLy). The curator nulled the extent; the cluster mass, member count and the extent-derived angular/linear sizes go with it.

ctx:GalacticHalo.why: Globular clusters whose curated records teach MW.halo and cite the Harris (2010) catalog that this context rests on. M71 is left out: its curator places it near the disc, not in the halo. M54 stays in ctx:SgrDSph.

ctx:M81Group.why: spring-dso lists NGC2403 as a member; the object record lacked the back-link.

engineEvalFlags.notes: Data problems found by the engine evaluation (script/journeys/eval/run-grid.ts, docs/sky-journeys/engine-eval.md). Not read by the build; for the template / narration / curator owners. The engine works around each one as described in `engine`.

templates.problem: Slot superlativeTags use doc-04 forms (most-luminous-in-view, hottest-star-in-view, reddest-star, brightest-star, fastest-moving, fastest-spinning) while curators wrote most-luminous, hottest, reddest, brightest, fastest, fastest-spinner. youngest, coolest-star-in-view and largest-apparent match no KB object.
templates.engine: slotMatches compares tag stems (candidates.superlativeStem); A7 went from 0% to 14.5% of themed requests. Align the vocabularies at the source.

templates.problem: The hook slot 'Milky Way river' (milky-way-field / star-cloud, maxObsDifficulty 2) has one qualifying object, M24; MWF-CygnusRift has difficulty 3. The payoff slot is labelled 'Another galaxy' but accepts globular clusters (M14 filled it).
templates.engine: A11 runs only around Sagittarius at a dark site (1.2% of themed requests). Add binocular Milky Way fields (Scutum Star Cloud, Large Sagittarius Star Cloud, Cygnus Star Cloud, Norma, Carina) and relabel or split the payoff slot.

templates.problem: 'Smoke ring' (pn, maxObsDifficulty 3) matches only M27; 'Shattered star' (snr) only the Veil (NGC 6960/6992) and M1, all challenge objects. No curated link joined a planetary nebula to a supergiant.
templates.engine: Derived CONTRAST 'mass decides the fate' (PN/white dwarf vs supergiant/SNR) and challenge payoffs where the slot allows maxObsDifficulty 4; A8 now runs at dark sites in summer (3.5% of themed requests).

templates.problem: Payoff 'Dying star' accepts any giant at evoStage 5-7, so Hyades giants (Ain, gamma and delta-1 Tauri), zeta Persei, zeta Aurigae and Arneb close the story as dull payoffs.
templates.engine: payoffTerm weights wow and difficulty; consider minWow 3 or roles [supergiant, pn, snr] for the payoff.

templates.problem: Payoff 'Blue-hot star' (teffK >= 9000) admits white A stars such as Merak and Phecda as the hot end of the thermometer.
templates.engine: Colour archetypes now only use stars of mag <= 6 (STAR_COLOR_MAG); consider teffK >= 10000 or minWow 3 for the payoff.

templates.problem: Archetypes with a fact progression accepted any CONTRAST/SCALE link, e.g. a distance ladder stepping by star radius.
templates.engine: themeLinkOk (no data change needed): fact-bearing links must be about the progression fact and go its way.

templates.problem: Template maximum lengths are 5-8 stops (A10 [3,5], most [4,6]-[4,7]), so the UI's 'Long: 7-10 stops' request is mostly met by relaxing the length: at 8 stops asked, 1,766 of 2,076 grid journeys were 3-7 stops and only 333 took the archetype switch.
templates.engine: Relaxed lengths now rank by closeness to the request (LENGTH_MISS_COST). Raise slot repeat ranges / template lengths, add switch targets, or relabel the Long option.

templates.problem: Without a progression or binary/variable-specific derived links, many steps ride derived luminosity or radius contrasts (true, but not about doubles or variability).
templates.engine: Derived SAME_PHYSICS must share a core concept; more curated SAME_PHYSICS / SAME_FAMILY edges between doubles and between variables would carry these themes better.

narration.problem: Every SCALE / TIME_MACHINE variant climbs ('Next rung', 'Keep counting', 'Older light'); a step back toward us (into a coda, or out of A11's distant star-cloud hook) has no text.
narration.engine: narrate.ts uses the direction-neutral CONTRAST.<fact> lines, then a built-in 'Back the other way' line.

narration.problem: Key of the new derived fate contrast has no bank variants.
Two variants read 'about {ratioPhrase} wider/farther' while ratioPhrase already says 'about N times wider'.
narration.engine: tidyText repairs it at runtime; fix the source lines.

narration.problem: The first generic variant ('{next} is what a family like {prev} grows into') assumes two clusters; it is also picked for star to planetary nebula steps (Albireo to the Dumbbell).
narration.engine: None; add LIFE_NEXT.<evo>-<evo> variants for star steps or make the generic lines kind-neutral.

narration.problem: Variant 'Birth or death: how can two glowing clouds mean opposite things?' assumes two nebulae, but A6 journeys are often all stars.
narration.engine: None; question / hook variants must fit every journey the archetype can build.

objects.problem: variability.binocularVisibleAtMin is false (Mira, chi Cygni, R Leonis, R CrB ...), but mag holds the maximum.
objects.engine: conditions.fadingFloor rates them at least 2: at most the one challenge stop, never the opener, stop 2 or a payoff.

objects.problem: Star records carry the cluster role 'young-cluster' (Alcyone, 15 Monocerotis), so a single star fills cluster slots such as A12 'Bright family' or A1 'Newborn family'.
objects.engine: None; keep cluster roles on the cluster records (membership lives in contextIds and edges).

objects.problem: Curated SIBLING 'member-star' / CAUSE 'dominant-star' edges join a cluster or nebula to a star inside it: the same binocular view.
objects.engine: StoryGraph.pairOk never puts both in one journey (only a curated LINE_OF_SIGHT, e.g. Aldebaran and the Hyades, justifies a star inside a deep-sky object's extent). The edges remain useful for cards and context.
